family.title: Wellness for every life stage

cards.name: Individuals
cards.detail: Align sleep stages, daily movement, and recovery on one timeline so you can see how each day’s rhythm shifts—not just isolated numbers.

cards.name: Households
cards.detail: One account links multiple family members. You choose what to share so alerts and trends arrive as one trusted narrative, not scattered screenshots.

cards.name: Seniors
cards.detail: Built for aging-in-place: vitals and safety signals can notify trusted contacts with clear context—what changed, and who should act.

cards.name: Chronic care
cards.detail: Long-horizon curves for BP, weight, and heart rate sit next to follow-up milestones so visits start from shared context, not guesswork.

cards.name: Workplace
cards.detail: Programs for teams and institutions with aggregated insight and minimal identifiers—useful statistics without exposing who is who.

cards.name: Ecosystem
cards.detail: APIs and SDKs let partners ingest rhythm summaries into the apps and services you already use—connected, consent-first, and interoperable.

family.ctaIntro: From one person to the whole household, Awak Health turns fragmented signals into one trustworthy language you can act on every day.

b1.title: Awak Health Spring 2026 keynote recap
b1.subtitle: Where tech meets aesthetics
b1.excerpt: Full recap: new wearables matrix, Awak Health Cloud updates, and the open-stack roadmap—plus how rhythm data turns into actionable guidance.

b2.title: The art of breathing
b2.subtitle: A chat with our Chief Health Officer
b2.excerpt: From breath and rhythm to signals you can track—without losing the human side, with practice tempos you can reuse in daily training.

b3.title: City cycling initiative
b3.subtitle: Connecting communities by route
b3.excerpt: Partnering with riders and cities to map healthier mobility networks so commuting, social rides, and light training share one timeline.

b4.title: The future of inclusive design
b4.subtitle: Technology that serves everyone
b4.excerpt: Accessibility in interaction, type, and feedback—shipping into the next generation, with reusable component specs and QA checklists.

b5.title: Materials lab
b5.subtitle: Finding gentler ways to wear all day
b5.excerpt: Skin-friendly wear tests and durability learnings from our first materials sprint, plus the next batch of candidates and ergonomics studies.

b6.title: Global sleep research summit
b6.subtitle: Inside deep sleep
b6.excerpt: Working with researchers on staging and recovery—rolling into the next model release, with notes on explainable staging from the floor.

b7.title: Ecosystem partners
b7.subtitle: Building an open blueprint for digital life
b7.excerpt: Entry paths for developers and institutions—programs, APIs, and compliance guidance so you can choose SDKs, webhooks, or bulk exports.

b8.title: Clinical collaboration white paper
b8.subtitle: Wearable vitals and remote follow-up
b8.excerpt: Joint guidance from hospitals and research partners on using wearable vitals outside the clinic—sampling cadence, alerts, and audit trails.

b9.title: Winter sports safety guide
b9.subtitle: Rhythm and load in cold weather
b9.excerpt: How heart rate, temperature, and training load couple in the cold—practical tips for outdoor runs and ski days so early warnings stay readable.

technology.title: Multimodal sensing & on-device compute
technology.description: Optical, inertial, bioelectric and ambient signals share one low-power pipeline—noise suppression and feature extraction happen locally, then high-confidence rhythm summaries sync to the cloud. You see conclusions, not raw waveforms.
